The words of Executive Order 11708 are in the present tense, so the revocation was performed by the order itself and was executed and exhausted when the order was signed on 1973-03-23; EO 11248 stayed in force only for the positions enumerated in Section 2. The later supersession of EO 11708 by EO 11768 on 1974-02-20 is not the first end of this clause, because a later supersession does not prove first cessation of a command already performed, and the held text of EO 11768 does not revive EO 11248. The surviving effect (EO 11248 revoked, except for the Section 2 positions) is described in the savings statement.

Section 1 of Executive Order 11812 (signed October 7, 1974; 39 FR 36307) adjusts upward the rates of monthly basic pay for members of the uniformed services in the printed tables, under section 1009 of title 37 and the Federal Pay Comparability Act of 1970 named in the enacting words. The order took effect October 1, 1974 (Section 6; paraphrased because the held OCR of that sentence is garbled). The rates ran until Executive Order 11883 of October 6, 1975 (40 FR 47091, Federal Register of October 8, 1975) superseded the order. EO 11883 Sec. 5 provides that Executive Order No. 11811 and "Executive Order No. 11812 of October 7, 1974, are hereby" superseded, and EO 11883 Sec. 4, Effective Date, provides that the adjustments in monthly basic pay and basic allowances for uniformed-services members "shall be effective on October 1, 1975." Section 5 gives no separate effective date for the supersession, so it is read with Section 4: the replacement uniformed-service rates apply from 1975-10-01 and the superseded rates are replaced from that date, which is recorded as the first end. The alternative reading, that the supersession operated on the signing date 1975-10-06, is stated for the reviewer; the rates paid for 1975-10-01 to 1975-10-05 are in either case those of EO 11883. It restates the limit that 5 U.S.C. 5308 itself imposes, which the footnotes of the Section 1 tables also repeat; the statutory limit continues by statute, but the order's own command is part of the superseded order and ended with it. No held source shows the limit was lifted or changed earlier. EO 11883 Sec. 5 provides that Executive Order No. 11811 and "Executive Order No. 11812 of October 7, 1974, are hereby" superseded, and EO 11883 Sec. 4, Effective Date, provides that the adjustments in monthly basic pay and basic allowances for uniformed-services members "shall be effective on October 1, 1975." Section 5 gives no separate effective date for the supersession, so it is read with Section 4: the replacement uniformed-service rates apply from 1975-10-01 and the superseded rates are replaced from that date, which is recorded as the first end. The alternative reading, that the supersession operated on the signing date 1975-10-06, is stated for the reviewer; the rates paid for 1975-10-01 to 1975-10-05 are in either case those of EO 11883. First end 1975-10-01 by express supersession.

reason: Section 5 lists seven earlier Executive Orders on uniformed-service pay (Nos. 11414, 11475, 11525, 11577, 11638, 11692 as amended, and 11740) and provides that they are hereby superseded. The act is performed in the present tense by the order itself and the order is dated October 7, 1974, so the clause was executed and exhausted when the order was signed on 1974-10-07; Section 6 makes the order effective retroactively from October 1, 1974, and the alternative reading, 1974-10-01, is stated for the reviewer (the signing date is used because a first end cannot precede the order's own date). The later supersession of EO 11812 by EO 11883 on 1975-10-01 is not the first end of this clause, because a later supersession does not prove first cessation of a command already performed. EO 11883 does not name or revive any of the seven orders; their supersession is an accrued effect described in the savings statement.

reason: This clause is the whole operative paragraph of Executive Order 12162 of September 28, 1979: by the authority of the Constitution, the statutes and the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973, Executive Order No. 12140 is, in the words of the held text, "hereby amended by deleting the first sentence in Sec. 1-105." The act is performed in the present tense by the order itself, so the clause was executed and exhausted when the order was signed on 1979-09-28. The deleted sentence was the sunset of EO 12140 (midnight on September 30, 1979), so the order took effect before that sunset could run. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986) later orders that the Executive Orders it lists, and their amendments ("any amendments thereto, are revoked:"), are revoked, and its table includes 12162; the held text states no effective date later than signing and no exception, so that revocation operated from 1986-02-25. It is a later event, not the first end of this clause, because a later revocation does not prove first cessation for a command already performed. The surviving effect of the amendment is described in the savings statement.
